Scope: roads and paving, potable water, TSE, sewer, storm water, irrigation and landscaping, electrical (medium voltage, telecom, street lighting) and CCTV networks in Zones A and G, over 18 months.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. On 16-Nov-2026 the project is 50.2% complete against 48.6% planned, 1.6% ahead (SPI 1.03). This week it gained 2.35% against 2.76% planned (85% of the plan), so the lead narrowed from 2.0% to 1.6%, the fifth weekly drop in a row. Storm water and electrical works earned most of the week's man-hours. The storm water, sewer, TSE and potable water networks are ahead; road works are now 0.3% behind, and procurement, engineering, electrical works and CCTV are further behind. The schedule update now forecasts completion 153 days after the contract date.

Ahead on progress, but the schedule update now finishes 153 days late. The P6 update of 16-Nov-2026 and the weekly report both forecast completion on 05-Dec-2027, 153 days after the contract date of 05-Jul-2027; last week both still showed 05-Jul-2027. The most negative float in P6 (−154 days) is on the unit substations: the distribution substation and transformer approvals have not started, so the purchase order and delivery (now to 24-Feb-2027) are late. All network works now complete on 30-Sep-2027 (float −76 days). Procurement is still at 60.4% against 100% planned (SPI 0.60): MV cables (0 of 51,500 m), unit substations, street lighting poles and lighting panels are not delivered, and the final substation location is still pending between the Client and SEC.

Data notes

  • The uploaded files name the project "Phase Two – Part Two" (SUD1-02-011), while the repository folder and the project tracker call it Phase 3 (المرحلة الثالثة).
  • The summary sheet labels cost-based progress as "Plan" and "Actual". This report uses physical progress (man-hour weighted) only: 48.65% planned and 50.22% actual.
  • The Physical-Chart Data sheet's baseline plans 52.5% at 06-Nov, above the 48.65% planned to 16-Nov on the front sheet, and it shows the 16-Nov actual (50.22%) on the 06-Nov point. Measured against that chart baseline the project would be behind plan.
  • The front sheet leaves physical progress for electrical, landscape and CCTV works blank; the man-hours in the Progress sheet were used. The Progress sheet's PW Planned / PW Actuals block still shows last week's values. The front sheet's BOQ values for CCTV Zone A and Zone G read 46,056 and 2 SAR instead of 6,513,996 and 2,791,854. TSE now has 60 planned man-hours to date (0.07%), which gives an SPI of 137; it is shown as – in the phase table.
  • The P6 update has the same data date as the weekly report (16-Nov-2026), but its activity counts (898 completed, 350 in progress, 867 not started) differ from the Schedule sheet (900, 348, 867), and the front sheet still shows 144 in progress.
  • In the P6 update the project finishes on 05-Dec-2027, 153 days after the contract date, but its float is −132 days, and 96 open activities (mostly potable water, TSE, sewer, storm water and irrigation) are scheduled to finish after 05-Dec-2027, the last on 18-Apr-2028. Last week no open activity finished after 05-Jul-2027.
  • Both files changed actual milestone dates this week: baseline submission from 06-Apr to 05-Feb-2026, and technical submittals to 05-Mar-2026 (from 25-Jul in P6 and 16-Aug in the weekly report); the weekly report moved mobilisation from 05-Feb to 06-Apr-2026. The weekly report now uses the approved baseline for the procurement phase (21-Nov-2026).
  • The summary page's scope table shows 0 executed for every network, and its totals differ from the hidden Conclusion sheet (for example roads 15,234 m vs 18,252 m). Manholes are labelled "m" in the Major Quantities sheet but are counted in units.
  • Procurement figures disagree: street lighting poles are 590 units and 10% complete in the Procurement sheet but 592 units with 1 delivered in Major Quantities; LV cables are 29,700 m vs 68,400 m. MV cables are "not submitted" in procurement, while the risk register says they have been procured.
  • November planned head count is 391 in the monthly table (365 manual, 26 non-manual) but 390 in the head-count panel (350 manual, 40 non-manual). Planned equipment in the Manpower sheet fell from 250 to 152 this week (dump trucks from 120 to 32).
  • Several cells show #REF! errors (EAC, risk scores, safety score in the status score). The substation risk carries a value of 6,835,460.61 SAR, which is the landscape BOQ value.
  • The issue log repeats entries: ID 3124 is used twice (observations 23 and 25), and the rain-water and road-diversion observations of 14 and 15-Nov are each logged twice; the risk register repeats them in the same way.
  • Several sheets (front sheet header, Major Quantities, Physical-Chart Data) still carry 19-Oct-2026 as their date, the Milestones sheet 09-Oct-2026 and the safety statistics and Testing sheets 09-Nov-2026, although the report's data date is 16-Nov-2026. The Major Quantities sheet is unchanged from 09-Nov and the Procurement sheet from 26-Oct. The Testing sheet gives 20-Apr-2026 as the forecast start of CCTV and MV testing. The report week is the contract week the report states (45 of 78); whole weeks since handover give 44.
